records.text: Mike Pompeo discussed options to take out Julian Assange.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Yeah, he discussed options to take out Assange just to make sure we were above bar there.

verification.notes: A detailed investigation citing more than 30 former U.S. officials reported that under Pompeo the CIA sought options for kidnapping Assange and that senior officials discussed possible assassination. This supports the statement, but confidence is medium because the underlying deliberations remain classified and public confirmation rests on unnamed former officials.

records.text: Mike Pompeo was arguing that future history books should omit the killing of Palestinian civilians because it harmed the intended narrative.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: he is sitting down and discussing how in the future they're just going to have to edit out of textbooks for kids that are in school. The part about how they murdered tens and thousands of Palestinian women and children and innocent men because it's just not good for their aims.

verification.notes: The clip confirms Pompeo said history books should not frame Gaza as the victim and should identify Israel as the victim and Iran/Hamas as aggressors. But he immediately acknowledged that there were victims and civilian casualties in Gaza. Owens's paraphrase captures his desired historical framing but overstates it as omitting the killing of civilians because it harmed a narrative.

sources.title: Pompeo: 'We Need to Make Sure' History Books 'Don't Write About Victims of Gaza'
sources.relevance: Provides the recorded remarks, including Pompeo's acknowledgment of Gaza victims and his preferred victim/aggressor framing.

records.text: Future history books should not describe Gazans as the victims; they should identify Israel as the victim and Iran and Hamas as the aggressors.
records.speaker: Mike Pompeo

appearances.snippet: it's not that we don't forget. We need to make sure that the story is told properly so that when the history books write this, they don't write about the victims of Gaza, right? They can't. I should be a little more precise. There were victims in Gaza, right? It's true. There are civilian casualties in every war that's ever been fought. But the victims were the people of the nation state of Israel, though that the aggressor was the Iranian regime in the proxy of Hamas. And we need to make sure that the history books reflect that. And that requires each of us every day to talk about it in real time with our children, with our grandchildren, about it in a way that is serious and thoughtful and complete and moral.

verification.notes: Verified as an attributed opinion, not as an objective judgment about the conflict. In the primary clip played in the episode, Mike Pompeo said history books should not write about 'the victims of Gaza,' then clarified that civilian victims did exist in Gaza but argued that Israel was the victim and that Iran and Hamas were the aggressors. The source statement accurately captures the position he expressed, while his clarification is important context.
